blocks.content:
A High Court is the highest judicial authority at the state or union territory level.

Each state has a High Court, but Parliament may establish a common High Court for two or more states.
A High Court is the highest judicial authority at the state or union territory level.

items: Parliament—and not the State Legislature—holds the exclusive power to establish a common High Court for two or more states.
High Courts represent the highest tier of the judiciary within a State or Union Territory.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The High Court serves as the apex judicial authority at the state or union territory level.
Each state individually has a High Court.
Parliament is constitutionally authorized to establish a single common High Court serving two or more states.
